summary.oneLiner: Delhivery delivered a bellwether FY26 with >1B parcels shipped and a decisive pivot to free cash flow positivity (Rs 89 Cr) one year ahead of schedule, driven by record volumes in Express/PTL and a margin turnaround in Supply Chain. The core thesis shifts from growth-at-all-costs to capital-efficient scaling, with ROIC expanding to 16% and net working capital compressing to 11 days, validating the operating leverage of the integrated network.

one-line thesis: Delhivery delivered a bellwether FY26 with >1B parcels shipped and a decisive pivot to free cash flow positivity (Rs 89 Cr) one year ahead of schedule, driven by record volumes in Express/PTL and a margin turnaround in Supply Chain. The core thesis shifts from growth-at-all-costs to capital-efficient scaling, with ROIC expanding to 16% and net working capital compressing to 11 days, validating the operating leverage of the integrated network.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Rs 10,486 Cr (FY26), Rs 2,848 Cr (Q4); EBITDA: Rs 764 Cr (7.3% FY26), Adj. EBITDA margin 6.3% (Transport), 10.9% service EBITDA (SCS); PAT: Rs 347 Cr (FY26, 3.2% margin), Rs 87 Cr (Q4); Order Book: Healthy SCS pipeline with 2 new mandates activated in Q4; Net Debt: Net Cash position >Rs 4,500 Cr. One-offs: Integration expenses for Ecom Express factored in yet FCF remained positive; no major accounting distortions noted.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Express volume grew 72-73% YoY in Q4; Margin: Express targeting 16-18% normative range, PTL margins expanding sequentially; Order Inflow: SCS pipeline margin-accretive with strict hurdle rates; Capex: Intensity reduced to 4.7% of revenue, targeting ~4% going forward, unaffected by AI/robotics pilots.
order book & pipeline: SCS business turned profitable with Rs 79 Cr service EBITDA (4x YoY); 2 new mandates signed/activated in Q4; Pipeline described as 'healthy' and focused on consumer durables, auto, and lifestyle sectors with disciplined client selection.
segment / subsidiary detail: Express: Rs 1,832 Cr revenue (Q4), +46% YoY, 306 Mn volumes; PTL: Rs 622 Cr revenue (Q4), +20% YoY, 2 Mn metric tons (FY26); Transport Combined: Rs 2,453 Cr (Q4), 7.9% adj. EBITDA margin; SCS: Rs 729 Cr (FY26), margin pivoted from 2.2% to 10.9% service EBITDA.
growth verticals / optionality: New verticals funded by core cash flows: Local delivery, Cross-border logistics, Rapid (quick commerce enablement), and Financial services; Tech moat via Delhivery Labs deploying LLMs, AGVs, and automation to reduce unit costs and labor dependency.
margins & cost dynamics: Fuel price hikes (~Rs 3/liter) being passed through via indexed contracts (DPH clauses) and air surcharges; Q4 margins expanded despite fuel headwinds due to network productivity gains; Labor cost inflation mitigated by automation (AGVs, robotics) and AI-driven claims/documentation efficiency.
capex / expansion: FY26 Capex intensity at 4.7% of revenue (down from 7.8% in FY23); Targeting ~4% run-rate; Investments focused on mega-gateway automation (AGVs, sorters) and tech stack; No material increase expected from AI inference or robotics scaling.
capital allocation: Disciplined organic investment in tech/automation and new verticals; Strong balance sheet (Rs 4,500 Cr cash) enables potential inorganic opportunities; Focus on ROIC expansion (now 16%) and sustaining free cash flow generation.
risks & watch-items: Fuel price volatility impacting consumption; Regulatory changes on gig-worker wages; Competitive intensity from marketplace 1P logistics (though management views 3P as structurally cheaper); Execution risk in scaling new verticals (cross-border/financial).
management quality / tone: Confident and disciplined; Emphasis on 'profitable growth' and 'capital efficiency'; Celebratory of hitting FCF positive early; Pragmatic on competition (dismisses Amazon 3PL threat as 'old news'); Forward-looking on automation to counter labor tightness.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly states that 1P logistics is structurally more expensive than 3P even after margins, suggesting a long-term structural shift of volume back to 3P as marketplaces face regulatory/labor cost pressures; The 'Delhivery Direct' app is quietly capturing significant SME/D2C share outside of aggregator channels; FCF positivity achieved despite full-year Ecom Express integration costs.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising fuel costs and labor wages squeezing logistics margins industry-wide | Delhivery Limited | beneficiary | High | Superior pass-through mechanisms (indexed contracts) and AI-driven cost reductions allow Delhivery to protect margins better than smaller peers; FCF inflection de-risks the equity story. |
| Marketplaces (Amazon/Flipkart) facing higher 1P logistics costs due to new gig-worker laws and minimum wage hikes | Delhivery Limited | beneficiary | Med | Structural cost disadvantage of 1P networks vs 3P will likely force marketplaces to shift more volume to third-party providers like Delhivery to optimize P&L. |
| Smaller 3PL players lacking capital for automation and tech moats face margin compression | Unorganized Logistics Players | loser | Med | Delhivery's scale and Rs 4,500 Cr cash pile allow aggressive investment in AGVs/AI that smaller players cannot match, widening the cost gap. |

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Reach is framed by coverage: 18,810 pin-codes served in Q1FY27, defined by the deck as unique pin-codes out of the 19,500 pin-codes as per India Post on which at least one shipment was delivered during the period (18,857 in Q1FY26; 18,830 in Q4FY26).
- 220+ countries and territories served (through Delhivery and partner networks), unchanged across Q1FY26, Q4FY26 and Q1FY27.
- Customer base described as 54,096 active customers in Q1FY27 versus 43,022 in Q1FY26 — active customers being those where an invoice was raised at least once during the quarter, excluding the count of Delhivery direct customers.
- The business is presented across five reported service lines: Transport (Express + PTL), Supply Chain Services, Others (Full truckload and Cross border), New initiatives (Delhivery Local, Rapid and Financial services), and corporate.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Ecom Express] The deck repeatedly carves out integration costs of the acquired Ecom Express business, quantified as ₹90 Cr for Q2FY26, ₹35 Cr for Q3FY26, ₹22 Cr for Q4FY26, ₹17 Cr for Q1FY27 and ₹148 Cr for FY26, described as net temporary costs pertaining to infrastructure, people, overheads, and business to be discontinued.
- [Ecom Express] Revenue from services in the service-line profitability table is stated to exclude revenue from Local, Rapid and Financial services, and Ecom Express businesses being transitioned — signalling that part of the acquired book is being wound down rather than retained.
- [Restatement basis] The quarterly income statement presents 'mgt. est.' columns for Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 that exclude the impact of Ecom Express related integration cost, so two different sets of figures for the same quarter appear in the deck (e.g. Q4FY26 revenue from services of ₹2,850 Cr reported versus ₹2,848 Cr on a management-estimate basis).
- [One-time items] Supply Chain Services FY25 adjusted EBITDA of ₹(64) Cr is attributed to a one-time impact of provisions on account of contractual matters, and Q2FY25 includes a reversal of ₹21 Cr of vendor advance provisions on account of settlement in our favour.
- [Associate] The income statement carries a separate 'share of profit / (loss) of associate (net)' line — ₹(3) Cr in Q1FY27, ₹9 Cr in Q4FY26 and ₹(8) Cr in Q1FY26 — but the deck does not name the associate.
